title: Starship deployment
description: A station a character takes aboard a ship, and the track of features they gain by serving in it. A deployment is levelled in ranks rather than in character levels, so it advances independently of a character's class: a 9th-level scoundrel who has flown two campaigns is a 3rd-rank pilot. Each rank grants a venture as well as the features listed here, which is why the starship-venture type exists separately.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this deployment. Ventures name deployments by this key's display name, so it is derived once and never reused.

name.description: Display name, singular, as a player would say it at the table: Gunner, not Gunners.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this deployment was published in, matching a document of the source content type.

contentSet.description: Whether this belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.

role.description: One line saying what the station actually does aboard the ship, which is what a player picking a deployment reads first. This is the archive's own summary line, not an editorial one.

rankProgression.description: The rank table printed at the head of the deployment, one row per rank, in ascending order. It is the deployment's class table: it says what arrives when, and a sheet reads it rather than the prose.

rank.description: Rank in this deployment. Five is the ceiling in every printed deployment.

features.description: Names of the features gained at this rank, as the table prints them. Every rank grants a Venture, which is why that name appears in every first row.

The rules text behind the rank table, in printed order. Names should match the rank table and mostly do; where they differ the transcription is inconsistent with itself — the Mechanic's table calls its 2nd-rank feature Ship Technician and its own body calls the same feature Ship Mechanic — and both spellings are preserved rather than one being silently chosen. A feature that lists options, such as a deployment's manoeuvres, is one entry whose description carries the options as sub-headings.

description.description: Markdown rules text in second person, because it addresses the crewmember rather than the ship.
